original_target.title: Residual finiteness of complex hyperbolic hyperplane complements

full_original_statement:
Let $`n\ge2`$, let $`M`$ be a connected complete finite-volume complex hyperbolic manifold of complex dimension $`n`$, and let $`S\subset M`$ be a compact, possibly disconnected, embedded totally geodesic complex submanifold of complex dimension $`n-1`$.

Must $`G=\pi_1(M\setminus S)`$ be residually finite? Explicitly, for every $`g\in G\setminus\{1\}`$, must there exist a finite group $`F`$ and a homomorphism $`\rho:G\to F`$ such that $`\rho(g)\ne1`$?

The ambient manifold may be compact or noncompact; no arithmetic hypothesis is imposed. Components of $`S`$ are disjoint, as required for an embedded submanifold. The question asks for a proof for every such pair or a counterexample within this class.

sources.scope_comparison: Original Question1.5 is the exact complement target and its actual preceding results give relative/residual hyperbolicity, not finite quotients. Stover–Toledo Theorems1.1–1.2 require cocompact arithmetic simple-type lattices and concern central extensions; Corollary1.4 is pi1 of the punctured line-bundle total space O(D)^times, not M minus D. The unrelated OpenAI family252 announcement constructs a non-residually-finite torsion-free hyperbolic group, without the required complement realization in its catalogue statement. Its pinned PDF returned unsupported octet-stream, so its theorem body was not reverified here and is a recorded source gap, not an exact-match decision. No unrestricted complement resolution located.
